page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-384-metal is an x86_64 bare-metal server configured with 384 dedicated vCPUs. It features 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration is designed for compute-heavy workloads that require massive parallel processing capabilities directly on physical hardware without virtualization overhead.

The instance does not include any local NVMe SSD storage or integrated GPU hardware. All storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, the server does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning network configurations must account for external routing separately.

Given its bare-metal nature and high core density, the server offers high resource density for compute-bound tasks. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that scale horizontally across many cores but do not require large memory footprints per thread. Appropriate workloads include large-scale batch processing, high-performance computing, scientific modeling, and intensive CPU-based compilation tasks.
